judgeIntroSpeech: Counsel, you may begin your presentation.
AQuestions: Counsel, the trial judge saw and heard all the evidence in this case. Is it not the job of the trial judge to weigh the evidence and decide what conclusions to draw from the evidence?

You argue that the trial judge made some errors in the law and errors in the analysis of the evidence. Can you point me to the specific language of the trial judge which you say demonstrates those errors?
Counsel, could you tell me where you are in your factum?
The Respondent’s Factum takes a different view of the cases you rely upon. Can you tell me why the Respondent’s view of those cases is not correct?
Even if the trial judge did make the errors set out in your argument, would they have made any difference in the result at trial?  Do you not agree the case against the accused had some weaknesses?
RQuestions: Is it at least possibility that the trial judge used the wrong legal tests in this case, and if there is any uncertainty on this issue, should we not err on the side of caution and order a new trial?
Do you agree that that the accused engaged in reckless and dangerous activity which is deserving of some sort of criminal sanction?
Counsel, could you tell me where you are in your factum?
The Appellant’s factum takes a different view of the cases you are relying upon. Can you tell me why the Appellant’s view of those cases is not correct?
As you are aware, we are not bound by any precedents. Could you please tell the Court why we should follow the law in the main authorities that you rely upon?
